- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤ -0.33) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.  
- If model shows a sharp upward spike followed by a forecast drop, it often overshoots; cap the peak forecast at 10% above recent high.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–70), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of true values.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; apply a 1–2 day smoothing filter to sentiment-weighted forecast.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast with sentiment trend only if sentiment is consistent for 3+ days.
